# Smithy

> Smithy is an interface definition language (IDL) and set of tools for building clients, servers, and documentation for any programming language. Smithy models define a service as a collection of resources, operations, and shapes.

> Links point at the documentation source (.rst, .md, or an included .rst.template/.md.template partial), which preserves exact rules that a summarized web-fetch of rendered HTML can drop. When changing an existing model, consult the Evolving Models guide under Key references first - it explains which changes are backward compatible and which break customers.

- [Smithy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/index.rst)
- [Quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/quickstart.rst)

## Key references

> The pages most often needed when authoring or evolving a model.

- [Trait index (every trait, one page)](https://smithy.io/2.0/trait-index.html) - rendered index, since the .rst source is only a build-time directive
- [Evolving Models (backward compatibility guide)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/guides/evolving-models.rst) - how to change a model without breaking customers
- [Breaking change rules (breakingChanges trait member)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/spec/model.rst) - machine-checkable backward-compat rules for traits
- [Smithy IDL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/spec/idl.rst)
- [Selectors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/spec/selectors.rst)
- [Constraint traits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy/main/docs/source-2.0/spec/constraint-traits.rst)

## Examples

> Runnable projects. Start from the index, then the per-language example.

- [smithy-examples (index of all examples)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-examples/main/README.md) - quickstart, conversion, custom traits, projections, shared models, linting
- [Java examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-examples/main/smithy-java-examples/README.md)
- [Rust examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-examples/main/smithy-rs-examples/README.md)
- [TypeScript examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-examples/main/smithy-typescript-examples/README.md)
- [Kotlin examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-examples/main/smithy-kotlin-examples/README.MD)
- [awesome-smithy (community resources)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/awesome-smithy/main/README.md) - curated list of build tools, generators, and resources

## Code generators by language

> Pick the generator for your target language. Start with its README, then follow the project documentation for current protocols, features, and stability.

- [smithy-java](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-java/main/README.md) - codegen (Java): clients are stable; server modules are developer preview
- [smithy-rs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-rs/main/README.md) - codegen (Rust): client, server, and the AWS SDK for Rust; interfaces are unstable
- [smithy-kotlin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-kotlin/main/README.md) - codegen (Kotlin): client
- [smithy-swift](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-swift/main/README.md) - codegen (Swift): client
- [smithy-ruby](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-ruby/main/README.md) - codegen (Ruby)
- [smithy-typescript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-typescript/main/README.md) - codegen (TypeScript): client and server (SSDK), developer preview
- [smithy-python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-python/develop/README.md) - codegen and core modules (Python): unstable and not yet for production - see ROADMAP below
- [smithy-python roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-python/develop/ROADMAP.md) - current status and planned Python features

## Tooling

- [smithy-cli](https://smithy.io/2.0/guides/smithy-cli/index.html) - build, validate, diff, and select over a model
- [smithy-language-server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-language-server/main/README.md) - LSP: editor navigation and diagnostics
- [smithy-gradle-plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-gradle-plugin/main/README.md) - run Smithy builds from Gradle
- [smithy-vscode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-vscode/main/README.md) - VS Code syntax highlighting
- [smithy-intellij-plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smithy-lang/smithy-intellij-plugin/main/README.md) - IntelliJ language support
